metadata.notes: agy DOES raise tool-less blocking dialogs (workspace trust: 'Do you trust the contents of this project?', persisted to settings.json trustedWorkspaces; and MCP elicitation: ElicitationInteractionSpec{server_name,mode,message,requested_schema_json,url}). But none can reach the daemon: the trust gate blocks BEFORE agy mints the conversation dir/transcript, so no session exists yet; and no dialog of any kind is written as a step — across 103 real CLI conversations transcript.jsonl carries no interaction step type at all, the parser skips every SYSTEM step, and a tool-less dialog has no tool_calls for the one path the parser does read. daemon=incapable → frozen.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: incapable
driver_capability: ready (moot — frozen)

Route: frozen. No recipe is authored and the spec is meta-only.

## What the scenario pins

`ready → working → waiting` entered while a dialog that names NO tool call is on screen; the episode is carried by no tool call (none in flight at entry, none completing to end it); after the user answers, `waiting → working → ready`; and the session is STILL `ready` at the end of a ≥15s trailing idle.

## agent_supports: yes — two of the four named triggers ship in agy 1.1.18

All four triggers were checked; two exist, two are the wrong shape for this row.

**1. First-use trust prompt for the workspace — EXISTS.** The agy 1.1.18 binary carries the literal string `Do you trust the contents of this project?`, and its answer is persisted: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` holds a `trustedWorkspaces` array (47 entries on this host, every one a prior recording's staging cwd). This is not inferred from a symbol — irrlicht's own antigravity driver already has a dedicated arm for it, `dismiss_dialog_if_visible "$SESSION" 'trust the contents|trust this folder'`, added because the gate "BLOCKS the REPL until answered" and otherwise swallows the first `send` (driver-interactive.sh:249-266). It names no tool.

**2. Server-driven MCP elicitation — EXISTS.** agy is an MCP client with full elicitation support: `exa.cortex_pb.ElicitationInteractionSpec{server_name, mode, message, requested_schema_json, url}` sits in the `RequestedInteraction` oneof (alongside `permission`, `file_permission`, `ask_question`, `mcp`, `approval_interaction`), paired with `ElicitationInteraction{action, content_json}`; the wire surface `elicitation/create` and `notifications/elicitation/complete` is present, as are both modes (`client does not support "form" elicitation`, `client does not support "url" elicitation`, `URL must be set for URL elicitation`, `requestedSchema must not be set for URL elicitation`). agy reads `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` (present, empty on this host). An elicitation is raised BY the server and answered by the user; no agy tool call carries it.

**3. Sandbox / network-access confirmation — EXISTS but is the WRONG SHAPE for this row.** agy has `ProjectSettings{file_access_policy, internet_policy, sandbox_mode, auto_execution_policy}` and a sandbox story documented in its own preamble ("Standard Sandbox Mode (BypassSandbox: false): By default has read/write access to your workspace, but no network access and no access to files outside the workspace unless added explicitly by the user"). But the confirmation is delivered as a `PermissionInteractionSpec{resource: PermissionResource{action, target}, trigger_source, …}` answered by `PermissionInteraction{allow, scope, sandbox_override, …}`, with `unsandboxed(*)` as the grant action — i.e. it is attached to the tool call that wanted the escape (`run_command`). That is `tool-gate-permission-prompt` / `permission-gate-non-mutating-tool` territory, and the scenario explicitly forbids substituting it here.

**4. Auto-mode / settings review — NOT CONFIRMABLE.** The only candidate in the descriptor is `ApprovalInteractionSpec`, which is an EMPTY message with `ApprovalInteraction{confirm}`. No TUI string, no config key and no transcript instance names a trigger for it, so nothing is claimed either way.

## daemon_capability: incapable — three independent reasons, none of them a missing rule

**(a) The one trigger that demonstrably ships fires before a session exists.** agy mints the conversation directory and `transcript.jsonl` only AFTER the first user prompt lands (driver-interactive.sh's launch_repl: "agy mints the conversation dir + transcript only AFTER the first prompt lands, so there's nothing to resolve at boot"), and the adapter is transcript-first — `agent.FilesUnderRoot{Dir: cliBrainDir, ExtraDirs: [ideBrainDir], SessionIDFromPath: sessionIDFromPath}` keys the session on the `<conv-id>` brain directory. While the trust dialog blocks the REPL there is no conv dir, no transcript, and therefore no session row for irrlicht to move to `waiting`. This is not a missed transition; there is nothing to transition.

**(b) No dialog of ANY kind is written as a transcript step.** Across the 103 real CLI conversations in this machine's brain store, `transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`) carry exactly these step shapes: `USER_EXPLICIT/USER_INPUT`, `MODEL/PLANNER_RESPONSE`, `MODEL/{RUN_COMMAND, LIST_DIRECTORY, VIEW_FILE, CODE_ACTION, GREP_SEARCH, INVOKE_SUBAGENT, GENERIC}`, and `SYSTEM/{EPHEMERAL_MESSAGE, CHECKPOINT, CONVERSATION_HISTORY, SYSTEM_MESSAGE, ERROR_MESSAGE}`. There is no interaction, elicitation, approval or dialog step type. `parser.go`'s dispatch skips every `SYSTEM` step outright (`default: ev.Skip = true`), and the two branches it does read are keyed on a USER_INPUT prompt and on a `PLANNER_RESPONSE`'s `tool_calls` — the very thing a tool-less dialog does not have. So by construction there is no entry edge and no release edge for this row's episode.

**(c) No hook can carry it either.** `installedHookEvents = []string{HookEventStop}` (hookinstaller.go:133) — one event, turn end. The only agy event that could bracket a user-blocking interval is `PreToolUse`, which is deliberately excluded on the #1719 hazard (its result carries `decision: allow|deny|ask|force_ask`), and which in any case is a TOOL event that cannot fire for a dialog attached to no tool. The adapter's own residue note states the position plainly: "through hooks, antigravity is a working/ready adapter".

**Where a trace WOULD exist, and why that is a new Source rather than a fix.** The sibling conversation store `~/.gemini/antigravity{,-cli}/conversations/<conv>.db` has a `steps` table whose `status` column is agy's `CortexStepStatus`, and that enum carries a dedicated `CORTEX_STEP_STATUS_WAITING = 9` alongside `PENDING = 1`, `RUNNING = 2`, `DONE = 3`, `ERROR = 7`, `CANCELED = 6`, `GENERATING = 8` (decoded from the binary's EnumDescriptorProto; the mapping is confirmed against the real stores on this host — 938 rows at 3, 17 at 7, 6 at 2, 4 at 6, 1 at 8). The store also has a per-step `permissions` blob (31 of 966 rows populated). But that store is NOT a watched Source: the adapter watches the brain directories only, and `dbmetrics.go` opens the store on `turn_done` for the context-token count and the canonical model id alone. Reaching a live `waiting` from it means adding a polled Source with its own permission copy — new architecture, not a rule change — which is why this is `incapable` and not `bug`.

## driver_capability: ready (moot)

The antigravity driver implements `send/slash/wait_turn/keys/sleep/interrupt/exit_clean/restart/resume/sigkill/start_session/session` (only `reset_session` is stubbed), so a recipe for this row would need nothing ported. It is moot under a frozen route, and it is worth recording that the driver's existing trust-prompt arm exists precisely to DISMISS the one dialog this scenario would want to hold open.
caveats: The two triggers that exist are evidenced from the shipped binary, the persisted trustedWorkspaces list and irrlicht's own driver — NOT from a live run. Driving agy was out of scope for this assessment (its cached OAuth token on this host can be silently expired), so nothing here proves that an MCP elicitation is reachable from a plain `send` in a fresh CLI session, nor that the trust prompt can ever appear mid-turn rather than only at REPL boot. Since both readings route to frozen, the uncertainty does not change the disposition — but it is the reason confidence is 0.75 rather than higher.

The daemon verdict does NOT depend on which trigger is used: the transcript census (103 conversations, zero interaction step types) and the parser's SYSTEM-skip make every tool-less dialog invisible, so a future agy that raised such a dialog mid-turn from a `send` would still be unobservable.

VACUOUS PASS: a frozen cell has no phases, so it cannot pass hollowly — but the load-bearing environment property is worth naming for a future re-assessment. The trust prompt is only raised for a cwd that is NOT already in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json's trustedWorkspaces (47 entries on this host, all prior recording cwds). Anyone re-probing this trigger must use a genuinely fresh directory, or the dialog never appears and its absence will look like the agent lacking the feature.

Re-assess if EITHER of these changes: (1) agy persists a pending interaction as a transcript step — the shape to look for is a step whose status decodes to CORTEX_STEP_STATUS_WAITING (9) or PENDING (1) appearing in transcript.jsonl rather than only in the SQLite store; or (2) the antigravity adapter gains a polled Source over conversations/<conv>.db that reads steps.status live, which is the only place a tool-less waiting episode is recorded today.

sources.note: agy 1.1.18: the literal TUI string 'Do you trust the contents of this project?'; exa.cortex_pb.ElicitationInteractionSpec{server_name,mode,message,requested_schema_json,url} + ElicitationInteraction{action,content_json} in the RequestedInteraction oneof; elicitation/create and notifications/elicitation/complete; ApprovalInteractionSpec is an EMPTY message; ProjectSettings{file_access_policy, internet_policy, sandbox_mode, auto_execution_policy}; CortexStepStatus enum with WAITING=9, PENDING=1, RUNNING=2, DONE=3, CANCELED=6, ERROR=7, GENERATING=8
trustedWorkspaces: 47 entries, every one a prior recording staging cwd — the trust prompt is a real, answered, persisted CLI dialog, not a symbol

launch_repl L249-266: the trust gate 'BLOCKS the REPL until answered' and is auto-dismissed by dismiss_dialog_if_visible; the same block records that 'agy mints the conversation dir + transcript only AFTER the first prompt lands' — so no session exists while that dialog is up

ParseLine dispatches on USER_INPUT / PLANNER_RESPONSE / other MODEL steps and sets ev.Skip = true for every SYSTEM step; the only user-blocking-shaped input it can read is a PLANNER_RESPONSE's tool_calls, which a tool-less dialog does not have

census of all 103 CLI conversations: step types are USER_INPUT / PLANNER_RESPONSE / MODEL tool results / SYSTEM {EPHEMERAL_MESSAGE, CHECKPOINT, CONVERSATION_HISTORY, SYSTEM_MESSAGE, ERROR_MESSAGE} — no interaction, elicitation, approval or dialog step type exists

installedHookEvents = []string{HookEventStop} (L133); PreToolUse deliberately excluded on the #1719 hazard, and it is a tool event that could not fire for a tool-less dialog anyway — the file's own residue note: 'through hooks, antigravity is a working/ready adapter'

Source = agent.FilesUnderRoot over the two brain dirs only; the conversations/<conv>.db store — the one place CortexStepStatus WAITING is recorded — is opened on demand by dbmetrics.go for tokens + model, never watched

recipe.note: Route is frozen on daemon=incapable — no recipe authored. agy DOES raise tool-less blocking dialogs (workspace trust; MCP elicitation), but neither can produce an observable waiting episode: the trust gate blocks the REPL before agy mints the conversation dir and transcript, so no session exists yet, and no dialog of any kind is written as a transcript step (103-conversation census: no interaction step type; parser.go skips every SYSTEM step; a tool-less dialog has no tool_calls). Author an interactive recipe (a `send` that provokes a configured MCP server's elicitation, a `sleep` of at least 15s to let the dialog render, a `keys` answer, `wait_turn`, then a ≥15s trailing idle) ONLY once agy persists a pending interaction into transcript.jsonl — look for a step whose status decodes to CORTEX_STEP_STATUS_WAITING (9) — or once the adapter gains a polled Source over conversations/<conv>.db's steps.status. The driver needs nothing ported either way: send/sleep/keys/wait_turn are all implemented.
